concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: אור ישר (or yashar — direct light; the primary outward flow from giver to receiver when the receiver can absorb the teaching)
אור חוזר (or chozer — reflected/returning light; the light that bounces back to the speaker when the recipient cannot receive, via the impact of the words)
הכאה (haka'ah — the striking/impact; the act of words going out from the speaker and hitting the friend, which causes or chozer to return to the speaker)
יראת שמים (yirat shamayim — fear of Heaven; the content/context of the conversation that generates or yashar and or chozer)
מוח קטן (moach katan — small mind/limited intellect; the condition of the recipient who cannot receive the speaker's words, causing or chozer to precede or yashar)
התעוררות (hit'orerrut — spiritual awakening/arousal; what the speaker himself receives back via the or chozer, even when his friend is not aroused)
דיבור לחבר (dibur l'chaver — speaking to a friend; the act whose outward motion generates the haka'ah and or chozer)
הכאה בכותל (haka'ah ba-kotel — striking a wall; the physical analogy: just as a sound/object rebounds from a wall, so too words return to the speaker from the friend)
analysis_notes.gap_explanation: Torah #184 is a five-line teaching with zero bechina edges in torahData.js (the reference field 184 does not appear in the dataset at all). The source text uses the word 'bechina' explicitly twice: once in line 3 ('וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת אוֹר חוֹזֵר מַמָּשׁ' — 'this is literally the aspect of or chozer'), and once in line 5 ('וְזֶה בְּחִינַת אוֹר חוֹזֵר, שֶׁהוּא עַל־יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַהַכָּאָה' — 'this is the aspect of or chozer, which is through the aspect of haka'ah'). These explicit bechina declarations point to at least two bechina relationships: (1) הכאה ↔ אור חוזר (haka'ah is the bechina/aspect of or chozer — they share the same essential nature of rebounding/returning), and (2) the returning of words to the speaker ↔ אור חוזר (the experiential phenomenon IS or chozer). The eight concepts listed above are all present in the source text and are candidates for future bechina-edge additions when Torah #184 is formally encoded into the dataset.
analysis_notes.source_text_summary: Torah 184 teaches: When one person speaks to a friend about yirat shamayim, or yashar and or chozer are created. Sometimes or chozer precedes or yashar — when the recipient has a small mind and cannot receive the words: then before his friend receives from him (or yashar), he first receives from his friend, making or chozer come first. Even when a friend does not receive, the speaker himself can be awakened through the haka'ah — just as one who strikes a wall has the thing return to him, so words sent to a friend return to the speaker through the haka'ah of the words hitting the friend. Therefore, speaking to a friend can awaken the speaker even if the friend is not awakened at all, whereas speaking to oneself alone might have produced no awakening. This is the aspect of or chozer: it operates through the bechina of haka'ah, as explained in the Kabbalistic writings.
